purpose: Teach: 酵母/菜園/人影/たまらなく/敷き/知ったかぶる/恥じ/押せ

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、本気で、絶対、お父さん、絶対、パン作りの、絶対、酵母、絶対、自分で、絶対、育てたぞ、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: Gran, do you remember? When you were young, your father was absolutely serious about raising his own yeast for bread-making.
lines.style: Soft, nostalgic opening. Gentle reach backward in time. Warm curiosity underneath — inviting her to meet him in the memory. Unhurried pace, breath of tenderness on the question.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん。若い頃、本気で、絶対、お祖父ちゃん、絶対、菜園、絶対、お庭に、絶対、作ってくれたわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: Yes. Do you remember, dear? Your grandfather was so serious back then — he built us a whole vegetable garden right there in the yard.
lines.style: Matching his warmth with her own brightness. A small smile in the voice. Leaning into the shared past with ease and recognition. Gentle confirmation that she's traveled there with him.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、夜の道、絶対、人影、絶対、見えると、絶対、ばあさんと、絶対、ほっとしたぞ、覚えてる?本気for
lines.en: When we were young, do you remember? There were nights on dark roads when I'd see shadows, and I felt so relieved knowing you were there with me.
lines.style: Quieter now, more vulnerable. The admission sits delicately — he's sharing something that mattered. Slow pace. Slight catch of feeling on the word 'relieved.' Still searching her face for recognition.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、お祖父ちゃん、絶対、たまらなく、絶対、お酒、絶対、飲みたい日、絶対、ありましたわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: Oh, there were days when your grandfather wanted nothing more than to drink sake. Don't you remember, dear?
lines.style: Light, knowing laugh underneath the words. Affectionate teasing — she's gently calling out his wants without judgment. A glint of mischief in her tone, warmth holding it all together.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 昔は、本気で、絶対、和室に、絶対、敷き布団、絶対、お父さん、絶対、毎晩、絶対、敷いたぞ、覚えてる、ばあさん?本気で
lines.en: Back then, your father would lay out the futon every single night in the Japanese room. You remember that, Gran?
lines.style: Settling into domestic memory. Steady, observant tone — he's noticing and naming small, faithful acts. Slight emphasis on 'every night' — the reliability itself is the point. Patient rhythm, like laying something out carefully.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、お祖父ちゃん、絶対、知ったかぶる、絶対、こと、絶対、なくて、絶対、誠実だったわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: Your grandfather never put on airs, you know. He was so sincere. Don't you remember, dear?
lines.style: Warm affirmation wrapped in tender admiration. She's naming something she loved in him. Gentle pride in her voice — speaking of his character without strain. Small pause before 'sincere' to let it land.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、お父さん、絶対、失敗を、絶対、恥じる、絶対、ことなく、絶対、前向きだったぞ、覚えてる、ばあさん?本気で
lines.en: Your father never felt ashamed of failing. He was always looking forward. You remember that, don't you, Gran?
lines.style: More firm now, with quiet conviction. He's celebrating something essential about the man. Light emphasis on 'always' — the consistency was remarkable to him. Still warm, but with the weight of real observation underneath.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、ボタンを、絶対、押せば、絶対、お湯が出る、絶対、家電、絶対、新しくて、絶対、嬉しかったわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: Those new appliances were such a joy, remember? When you'd just press a button and hot water would come out. We were so happy about those modern things.
lines.style: Brightness in her voice — genuine delight in small technology, in comfort. Warm, almost girlish remembering. A soft laugh quality to it, as if the simple pleasure still moves her. Unhurried, lingering on the happiness.
